title: Some: faith only senses a justification already done before belief
source_text: IX. Quidam enim volunt fidem proprie non justificare, & justificationem fidei, nonnisi admodum improprie tribui: quia, scilicet, per fidem habemus sensum justificationis jam ante illam, & sine illa factae. Nam existimant justificationem esse aliquid quod fidem praecedit; & electos Dei justificatos esse, etiam antequam credant, & convertantur. Atque, quoniam ex eorum mente, justificatio vel ab aeterno facta est, vel saltem tum quum hominibus promissus est Christus Mediator, qui peccata nostra in se susciperet, & se pro nobis sponso rem justitiae divinae offerret; Itaque justificatio proprie accepta ipsis aliud non est, quam certa Dei voluntas de electis a peccato, propter Christum, absolvendis: nec, respectu hujus justificationis, fides aliam vim, aut officium habet, quam ut nos in ejus notitiam ducat, & de illa certos & securos reddat.
pass_a_gloss: For some want faith properly not to justify, and justification to be attributed to faith only quite improperly: because, namely, through faith we have the sense of a justification already made before it and without it. For they think justification is something that precedes faith; and that God's elect are justified even before they believe and are converted. And since on their view justification was either done from eternity, or at least when Christ the Mediator was promised to men, who would take our sins on himself and offer himself as surety of divine justice for us; therefore justification properly taken is for them nothing other than God's certain will concerning the elect being absolved from sin for Christ's sake: nor, with respect to this justification, does faith have any other force or office than to lead us into knowledge of it and make us certain and secure about it.
pass_b_english: Some say faith only senses a justification already done—eternal or at the promise of Christ.
On that view faith's only role is to make us know and feel secure about it.
